questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was mainly a connection of two things. Firstly, I choose Paris because I'm very interested in art and art history and I've always loved painting and drawing. Paris is in many ways the capital of art, with its numerous museums and rich history, why I saw it as a great way to explore my interest. Secondly, the living situation in Paris was a big plus. I had heard about the cite internationale universitaire Paris, which is sort of a campus for exchange students. This made it both much easier and cheaper to find a place to live in an otherwise very expensive city.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was a bit difficult. We got a mail about where to show up for the introduction week and for the welcome meetings, but other than that there were not much information. It was very step-by-step in the sense that we got more information as we needed it, but it would have been nice to have a bit more information up front as we all had many questions about course registration and other practical stuff beforehand.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
We had two welcome meetings. The first one was a welcome to the entire school regardless of the department. The meeting was an introduction to Sorbonne, how the school works and the different social offers. However, the entire meeting was in French and sadly, I don't speak a lot of French so I didn't understand much of it. 
The second meeting was a welcome for the economics department, where we got a general introduction to the school and the registration process. After the presentation, we could ask specific questions

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The cité internationale universitaire de Paris is sort of a campus for exchange students for all Paris universities. The cité is organised into foundations, which all have their own house. Typically a foundation is for a specific country, but there are also some different french ones. I lived in Fondation Danoise, which is the "danish house". You have to apply however, so you are not ensured a spot.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: The cooking facilities at Fondation Danoise was very good, with a big kitchen and fridge and storage space for each room. There is also a canteen in the cite internationale universitaire paris, but I didn't end up using it as the kitchen at Fondation Danoise was so well equipped.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The Fondation Danoise was a great place to live and I highly recommend applying. It's similar to a danish dorm, where you end up getting close to the other people living at the house, if you are just open to getting to know them. Most people living in the Fondation Danoise are danish, so the house feels very homey from the start. If you want to apply, do so in good time and spend some time on your application as many are interested.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I got a link to the registration webside, where I needed to input a bunch of different information about myself. It was fairly straight forward, as most of the information was standard identification or easy to find. I needed a few documents like a certificate for my language level and a signed online learning agreement. This online learning agreement caused a bit of trouble. I needed a course description to get the courses, I planned to take, approved, but as I was not enrolled into my host university yet, I could not access this description. I ended up having to talk to my home university so I could make a temporary online learning agreement, which was a bit of a hasle. After I was enrolled, I got another email so I could get an account for the host university webside.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I got help from my home university, which was really great and very quick. I also asked some of the former exchange students what they did and that helped a lot too. I also got help from the incoming student officer, when I arrived with registering to courses.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Registering for classes was done on a webside at a specific timeslot. As everybody tried to register at the same time, the webside became faulty and I could only register for half of the courses I wanted. The day after I went to the Incoming student officer, who enrolled me manually to the rest of my courses. I only had to change one course as the one I wanted was full, but other than that I got all the courses I had planned to take.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would try to make my online-learning agreement as soon as possible, so seek pre-approval as soon as you can as it can take some time. I ended up finding some course descriptions by going trough the university webside very carefully also looking at the pages only in french. When there were no description I looked if the course had been pre-approved before.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses were both easier and harder than at UCPH, but this was more due to the teaching style than due to the level. In general the level was a bit lower than at UCPH, as the courses were less focus on the specific mathematics of the models and more on a general understanding of the concepts instead. Furthermore, some of the courses were also intended for non-economics master students, why some basic economic theory needed to be covered and some of the models were simplified.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: All the courses consisted of 3-hour lectures with class discussions. The focus was very different from UCPH, as there were little to no formal calculations and only graphical representation of the models. Instead there were a great focus on concepts and being able to relate the models to each-other and real-life problems. As an example the exams was primarily essays and open-ended questions, which could make the courses harder if this is not your strong suit.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: I enrolled in 1) Labor Economics, 2) Industrial Economics, 3) Political Economy, 4) Development Macroeconomics and 5) European Integration.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend Labor Economics, Industrial Economics and European Integration. All of these courses were nicely structured, the lecturer was super clear and all the learning material was readily available. I also found them really interesting. The other two were less structured and it was hard to find the course material, so I didn't get as much out of them.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I did not account any unexpected costs besides some things being more or less expensive, as I had asked some of the former exchange students about their costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
My host university didn't use books much and if they did they provided the material so that was free. 
Grocery shopping is slightly more expensive than DK, where I expected it to be cheaper.
The metrocard is a bit more expensive than I expected, but it is still a good deal if you want to explore the city.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: As part of the introduction week you could sign up for a 5-day french course (4 hours each day). At the welcome meeting they presented a bunch of different the non-academic opportunities, including sport clubs and social activities. They presented it in french however, so it was a little difficult to figure out what all the extra curricular were. Furthermore, all the exchange students had a WhatsApp group, where social events were posted including parties, dinners, karaoke etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did not really participate in anything offered by the university. I mostly partook in events from Fondation Danoise.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Use the city. There is so much fun to do! For instance: the channels are super lovely in the sun in the 10 arrondissement, all the museums are free if you are below 26 or walk along the highline in Paris.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy, since I had been to France before and kind of new what to expect. Also France is a european country why we share a lot of the same culture and values.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Meet other people in the Cite. Go to parties and to you friends houses. It is the best way to meet people if you are open to meeting them.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Strikes. The french really like to strike. During my stay there were a change in the retirement age, which was a big debate and caused a lot of strikes affecting the transportation system and garbage disposal.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Going out. The French love to go out even on a regular week day and it makes the city very vibrant and alive.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1)Be prepared for the registration process. It can be very tedious at times and 2) remember to ask for help! 3) Apply for the city it is a great place to live even if you live at another house than the danish one.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The exam dates are released two weeks before the actual exam period starts. Don't stress about it. All the exams are by hand so practice your handwriting :)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The social life at the Cite and the danish house.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The registration process.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
